Subject: CloudBridge — post-demo tech recap & routing/ops qualification

Hi Alex / Priya — great demo earlier. Quick consolidated note for engineering + product to make next steps concrete. TL;DR: CloudBridge wants low-latency chat with an economical fallback, embeddings for reranking search results, and structured tool calling for a payments microflow.

Summary of requirements from today
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms target for short chat (90% of requests are < 100 tokens)
- Throughput: steady-state ~60 RPS; headroom for 250 RPS spikes (weekday peak)
- Data residency: US-only; no external KV stores allowed behind customer data plane
- Auth: prefer short-lived API keys for hosted; enterprise would consider mTLS for private deployment
- Routing/policy: prefer primary low-latency model for interactive, fallback to cheaper batched variant when cost or capacity constrained
- Embeddings: vectorize search candidates and apply reranker for top 10 — want overall 10–20% QA lift
- Structured output & tool calling: payments flow must return machine-parseable JSON and call an external webhook with a signed payload

Attachments: SLA matrix (redwood-sla-matrix.pdf) and integration checklist (integration-checklist.md).

Asks / next steps
1) Marcus, can you propose a concrete model-routing policy and recommended model variants (latency vs cost tradeoffs) we can send to CloudBridge tomorrow? Include estimated p95 token latency and cost per 1M tokens for each leg.
2) Monica, please confirm whether we can support embedding + reranker within hosted with guaranteed US-only storage or whether CloudBridge will need a Dedicated/Private deployment.
3) Alex/Priya: share traffic profile and any security questionnaires (I think Priya mentioned a SOC2 excerpt). I attached our SLA matrix for quick alignment.

Proposed follow-up: 30-min technical sync on Monday to finalize routing policy and auth approach. Please reply with availability.

Thanks — Rachel

Thanks Rachel — nice summary. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Latency SLO: 200ms p95 is correct for the interactive experience; anything under 150ms p95 is a big win for us.
- Throughput: 60 RPS steady; spikes to 250 RPS are expected during batch syncs. Most spikes are short (3–5 minutes).
- Data & security: we cannot allow Redwood-managed external KV or third-party persistent stores for customer data. Host embeddings inside a US-only enclave is fine.
- Auth: for POC we can use time-limited API keys; long-term we prefer mTLS or mutual-auth when we move to Private.
- Embeddings/rerank: we want embeddings to be computed at write-time and stored in our vector DB; Redwood can offer embedding vectors back to us (signed) or host a reranker endpoint if needed.

I attached a small traffic profile spreadsheet (cloudbridge-traffic-profile.xlsx). Also, we can share parts of our security questionnaire early next week.

Availability: Monday 11/9 — late morning PT works for Alex and Priya.

Rachel / team — rough technical plan below (ready to convert into a one-pager + JSON policy). Will run numbers on cost estimates and p95 latencies with ops today and post before the sync.

Recommendation (high level)
1) Model routing chain
   - Primary: redwood-lowlat-8q (optimized for sub-150ms token latency at short sequences) — route all interactive chat <=120 tokens here when p95 < 150ms.
   - Secondary (cost-fallback): redwood-slim-4q (batched, quantized) — route when: a) observed primary p95 > 180ms for >30s, or b) consumption-based cost threshold breach (configurable per-account e.g., spend burn-rate).
   - Tertiary (queuing/slow): redwood-bulk-2q — used for async/background work and large generation (>1024 tokens)

2) Policy rules (expressed as priority bullets — will deliver JSON)
   - If primary latency p95 > 180ms over a rolling 60s window, divert new short-chat requests to secondary with sticky fallback TTL=30s.
   - If overall cluster GPU saturation >85% and queue length >50, return a 429-suggested-retry with estimated wait; if Auto-burst enabled, allow limited bursting to secondary pool.
   - Region routing: enforce US-only endpoints (us-west-2 preferred); failover to us-east-1 only if us-west-2 capacity exhausted and customer approves cross-region fallback.

3) Embeddings + reranker
   - Strategy A (preferred for POC): Redwood returns embedding vectors in response; CloudBridge stores vectors in their DB. Redwood can provide a reranker endpoint that accepts top-N candidates and returns a reranked ordering (stateless, signed request/response).
   - Strategy B (Dedicated/Private): run embedding storage inside customer VPC; Redwood only provides model inference. Required for regulated customers who disallow external storage.

4) Structured output & tool-calling
   - Use function-calling / structured-output enforcement with explicit JSON schema. Redwood will validate model outputs against schema and return structured payload + error code if validation fails. For external webhooks (payments), we sign the callback with per-customer HMAC and include replay-protection nonces.

5) Auth & SDK setup
   - POC: short-lived API keys (TTL 1–6 hours) plus per-route signing for webhook callbacks. Easier to onboard.
   - Production (recommended for Private): mTLS + rotating client certs; RBAC at route/model level.

6) Observability & fallbacks
   - Trace tokens, per-request cost attribution, and automatic alerts for routing-policy flips. Can emit tracing hooks to CloudBridge's tracing collector via OTLP.

Next steps before Monday sync
- I'll produce a JSON routing policy snippet + cost/latency estimates for the three model legs.
- Monica: confirm hosting constraints for embeddings (can we guarantee US-only storage in hosted?)

If nothing else, propose Monday 11/9 11:00–11:30 PT for the tech sync.

— Marcus
